title: Slot Harmonizer: prefetch & KV-pinning policy for heterogeneous dialogue lengths
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Problem: We see tail latency regressions and intermittent OOMs for mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts with long responses and vice versa). The continuous batching scheduler currently treats slots uniformly which causes inefficient KV residency and GPU slab fragmentation when sequence-length variance is high. Goal: implement a slot harmonizer that pairs incoming requests into small cohorts by expected response length, applies an adaptive prefetch stride and KV-pinning policy, and coordinates GPU slab compaction to reduce fragmentation without increasing p50 latency. This ticket covers design, prototype, metrics collection, and a canary rollout for the harmonizer policy.
acceptance_criteria: p95 generation latency for mixed-dialogue benchmark decreases by >= 18% under production-like arrival rates
No increase (>1%) in p50 latency across steady-state traffic compared to baseline
OOM incidents on our staging fleet reduced to zero for the tested 95th-percentile memory pressure scenarios
KV cache hit-rate for follow-up tokens improves by >= 10% for long-response cohorts
Canary rollout plan exists and has automated rollback condition based on increased error rate or latency SLO violations
technical_notes: High-level approach: 1) Estimate response length at enqueue time using a light-weight predictor (existing length-hint model) plus heuristics from prompt tokens. 2) Maintain short-lived "harmonizer cohorts" (3-6 slots) that coalesce requests with compatible length hints to reduce KV churn. 3) Apply adaptive prefetch stride: small stride for short-response cohorts to avoid over-prefetching, larger stride for long-response cohorts to amortize kernel launches. 4) Introduce KV-pinning for cohort leaders: pin commonly-shared prefixes/KV shards for cohort lifetime, with soft eviction when GPU slab pressure exceeds threshold. 5) Integrate a GPU slab compaction hook triggered during low-utilization windows to defragment allocator and reclaim small free islands. Trade-offs: cohorting increases batching variance and may slightly increase head-of-queue wait time; KV-pinning reduces eviction churn but can raise transient memory pressure, mitigated by slab compaction and soft eviction thresholds.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flagged prototype to runtime canary branch. 2) Run A/B bench against mixed-dialogue production replay for 72 hours. 3) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automatic rollback if p95 latency regresses >10% or error-rate increases >0.5%. 4) Expand to 25% then 100% if stable. 5) Observe for 2 weeks and collect cost deltas.
